overall.sentence: The headline idea, that overdoped cuprates are Landau-BCS d-wave superconductors once dopant disorder is included, was argued earlier by the dirty d-wave program of Lee-Hone, Broun, Hirschfeld and co-workers (arXiv:1902.08286, likely the paper's ref. [29]); this Perspective is new in attributing the anomalies mainly to mesoscopic inhomogeneity amplified by the short coherence length, in the clean-versus-disordered YBCO contrast, and in its set of falsifiable predictions.

assessment.claim: 1: overdoped regime is a weak-coupling BCS superconductor on a Fermi-liquid normal state (crossover picture)
assessment.note: Lee-Hone et al. already concluded that overdoped LSCO and Tl2201 are described semiquantitatively by Landau-BCS 'dirty d-wave' theory (same question and system); new here is the crossover framing with Tθ >> Tc ≈ Δ0/2 as the organising criterion and the qualitative synthesis across probes rather than a quantitative t-matrix fit.

assessment.claim: 2: overdoped anomalies are extrinsic, from substitutional disorder amplified by the short coherence length
assessment.note: Pal et al. (cited as [5]) and Sulangi et al. (2503.20861, cited as [6]) simulate inhomogeneity from dopant disorder in overdoped cuprates (same question and system, computational method); the paper adds a cross-probe argument (stiffness, C/T, Drude weight, T-linear resistivity, gaps above Tc) and the YBCO contrast.

assessment.claim: 5: inverting the BCS gap equation on Bi2212 ARPES data gives a short-range pairing interaction ~4J that decreases with doping
assessment.note: Storey et al. (2007, not cited) solved the BCS gap equation with an ARPES-derived dispersion and found the pairing interaction must decline rapidly with doping, consistent with a magnetic interaction (same question and method); new here are the use of measured doping-dependent Bi2212 gaps, the magnitude estimate J ≈ 0.15 eV and the argument from the gap's k-dependence against a quantum-critical pairing mode.

assessment.claim: 6: cleaner overdoped cuprates should show an exponential Tc tail, Tθ >> Tc, Δ0 ≈ 2kBTc, a mean-field specific-heat jump and vanishing T-linear resistivity
assessment.note: Disorder-driven trends in stiffness, residual C/T and Tc were already expected in the dirty d-wave work (cleaner Tl2201 vs LSCO); the combined prediction set, the exponential tail and pressure-doped YBCO as the test were not found, but only one round of searches targeted the predictions, so no stronger grade is given.

positioning: The closest earlier work is the dirty d-wave program (Lee-Hone, Broun, Hirschfeld et al., arXiv:1704.04803, 1802.10198, 1902.08286, 2206.01348) and Maier et al. (arXiv:2004.13120), which already argued that overdoped cuprates fit a Landau-BCS description with weak dopant scattering and a pairing strength that falls with doping; the paper cites the first group as [28-30] only as pair-breaking theory and leaves them out of its list of overlapping approaches. What this Perspective adds, as the searches show, is an argument that mesoscopic inhomogeneity rather than effective-medium pair breaking explains the anomalies, the clean-YBCO versus Ca-YBCO comparison, and a list of disorder-dependent predictions. Its BCS-inversion estimate of the pairing interaction has an uncited precedent in Storey et al. (arXiv:0707.2239), and ARPES on overdoped Bi2212 (Valla et al., arXiv:1905.01370) already linked the vanishing coupling to the end of the dome. The paper makes no explicit 'first' claims, so no tier A or C items arise.

issues.claim: In an ideal, disorder-free hole-doped cuprate there is a crossover near optimal doping to an overdoped regime described by weak-coupling BCS theory on a Fermi-liquid normal state.
issues.headline: Dirty d-wave Landau-BCS work left out of the overlap list
issues.issue: Lee-Hone et al. (arXiv:1902.08286, apparently the paper's ref. [29]) and Maier et al. (arXiv:2004.13120, not cited) already argued that overdoped cuprates fit a Landau-BCS d-wave description once weak dopant scattering is included. The paper cites [28-30] only as pair-breaking theory and leaves them out of the list of studies that overlap its approach, so a referee from that community may say the headline is not new.

issues.claim: Inverting the BCS gap equation on Bi2212 ARPES data gives a short-range pairing interaction of magnitude consistent with magnetic exchange that decreases with doping.
issues.headline: Earlier gap-equation inversion from ARPES dispersion is not cited
issues.issue: Storey et al. (arXiv:0707.2239, 2007) solved the BCS gap equation with an ARPES-derived dispersion and concluded that the pairing interaction must decline rapidly with doping, consistent with a magnetic interaction. Valla et al. (arXiv:1905.01370, 2019) showed by ARPES on overdoped Bi2212 that the coupling weakens and vanishes where superconductivity ends. Neither is cited where the paper presents its inversion as a new step.

evidence.quote: it is possible to work backwards from observations of the gap function to draw incomplete but clear inferences on the nature of the interactions responsible for the pairing.
evidence.location: The nature of the mechanism, first paragraph

issues.fix: Cite Storey et al. 2007 and Valla et al. 2019 at the start of the inversion section and state what is new: measured doping-dependent gaps, the magnitude estimate J ≈ 0.15 eV, and the argument from the gap's k-dependence.

edit.before: it is possible to work backwards from observations of the gap function to draw incomplete but clear inferences on the nature of the interactions responsible for the pairing.
edit.after: it is possible to work backwards from observations of the gap function to draw incomplete but clear inferences on the nature of the interactions responsible for the pairing. (A related analysis using an ARPES-derived dispersion found that the pairing interaction must decline rapidly with doping [Storey et al., arXiv:0707.2239], and ARPES on overdoped Bi2212 shows the coupling vanishing where superconductivity ends [Valla et al., arXiv:1905.01370]; here we use the measured doping-dependent gaps to extract the magnitude of the interaction.)
